summary: Burst of 502/504s tied to runtime GC thrash and GPU driver resets during multi-tenant embedding burst
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 02:10–02:34 UTC customers (notably Acme Analytics on a dedicated pool) experienced a rapid rise in 5xx responses (502/504) from the API Gateway. Impact: Short-lived spike produced ~18% error rate for embedding requests (small payloads) from the customer, causing job failures and increased retries client-side. Environment: prod (us-east) Dedicated capacity pool id: dp-45. Observed behavior: API Gateway returned 502/504 while downstream runtimes showed frequent process restarts and repeated nvml driver resets. Metrics: upstream runtime restart rate spiked from baseline ~0.02/min to ~2.4/min; GPU reset errors (nvml) increased by ~120x; Python GC pause time histograms showed a large increase in long pauses. Steps to reproduce: 1) Concurrent embedding bulk of small requests (payload ~120 bytes) fan out to many replicas. 2) Prefetch layer coalescing disabled for this tenant due to earlier config; 3) Runtimes experienced increased memory churn during KV cache updates leading to GC activity and eventual process watchdog triggers. Logs/snippets: "runtime: restarted by watchdog: nvml: GPU reset (code 43)"; "gc: pause 1286ms - major collection"; "apigw: upstream closed connection (reset)". Expected behavior: No sustained 5xx floor during short-request bursts; graceful queuing and batching or backpressure rather than upstream restarts.

2026-03-12 02:25 - SRE (Liam): Observed correlated spikes in runtime restarts and nvml errors. Opening investigation; attaching live dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/rg-45?from=2026-03-12T02:00Z&to=2026-03-12T03:00Z

2026-03-12 03:05 - Engineering (Priya): Kernel-level trace shows repeated GPU driver resets triggered within the runtime after long GC pauses. Suggest throttling concurrency for the tenant as a stop-gap.
2026-03-12 04:10 - Support (Anika): Applied temporary rate cap and enabled coalescing flag for Acme; error rate dropped to <1% within 20 minutes.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Post-incident (Liam): Rolled runtime GC tuning and queued a follow-up change to autoscaler policy to avoid simultaneous worker restarts. Marking resolved after monitoring 24h stable.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: simple apigw overload - ruled out by low CPU on API gateway and no accept queue saturation.
Found root trigger: a cluster of very small embedding requests caused extreme KV cache churn in runtime (many small updates), increasing Python object churn and triggering frequent full GC cycles.
Full GC pauses (p99) increased from ~25ms baseline to ~1.3s during spike; these pauses overlapped with NVML calls leading to driver timeouts on some GPUs.
NVML stacktrace shows driver reset originated while runtime held GPU context during a long blocking GC; watchdog interpreted as unresponsive and restarted process.
Autoscaler behavior: when one worker restarted, load briefly redistributed causing other warm workers to hit similar GC patterns and cascade into multiple restarts (crashchain).

Mitigation validated: enabling request coalescing + tenant concurrency cap prevented the KV-churn pattern and reduced GC pressure. Temporary kernel pin (quantized variant) used to reduce nvml interaction frequency.
Related internal ticket for autoscaler behavior: INT-2042 (queued).
resolution: Applied immediate mitigations: (1) Enabled per-tenant coalescing for small-embedding requests; (2) Temporarily capped concurrent embedding requests for Acme to 60 RPS; (3) Deployed runtime GC tuning (increase young-gen threshold, reduce frequency of full GCs) and updated watchdog window to tolerate longer GC pauses; (4) Rolled back a recent aggressive autoscaler policy that simultaneously recycled workers. After mitigations error rate fell to <1% and runtime restarts returned to baseline.
follow_up_actions: Permanent change: Implement request-size-aware batching and automatic coalescing for embed workloads (tracking ticket: ENG-7182).
Autoscaler: Add staged recycle to avoid synchronized worker restarts (ENG-7150).
Monitoring: Add GC pause alerts tied to downstream NVML driver resets and automatic short-circuiting of NVML calls during extended GC pause (SRE-402).
Docs: Update runbook to include detection pattern (GC pause spike + nvml resets -> apigw 502s) and immediate mitigations.
